title: Multi-Jurisdictional Legal Identity Assurance for Capability Gating: A Design-Science Proposal for Tiered, Reusable Identity Assurance of Natural, Juridical, and Machine Entities
abstract: arXiv:2610.00287v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Identity assurance is the cost a digital system pays for dishonesty and uncertainty: it exists to make acts attributable when not everyone can be trusted at their word. A common way to pay that cost is flat maximum verification, asking each participant to meet a single high level of identification at entry, before any capability is exercised. Paid on everyone, it over-collects, excludes participants who cannot meet a bar they never needed to clear, taxes every interaction with the cost of the rarest high-risk case, and binds the strength of identification to the activity it unlocks. Existing frameworks compound this by fixing a small number of per-credential levels inside a single legal space and binding each verification to the institution that performed it, leaving cross-border reuse and the tension between data erasure and evidentiary retention unaddressed. This paper develops, as a design-science proposal, a tiered and reusable mod

translated_title: 面向能力准入的多法域法律身份保证：针对自然人、法人与机器实体的分层可复用身份保证的设计科学提案
translated_abstract: 身份保证是数字系统为不诚信与不确定性所支付的成本：它的存在是为了在并非人人皆可信其言之时，使各种行为可以被归责。支付这一成本的一种常见方式是“扁平化最高验证”，即要求每位参与者在进入时、在行使任何能力之前，就达到单一的高级别身份核验。由于这种成本由所有人承担，它会导致过度收集信息，将那些无法达到其实本不需要达到之门槛的参与者拒之门外，使每一次交互都背上最罕见高风险情形的成本，并将身份核验的强度与其所解锁的活动捆绑在一起。现有框架进一步加剧了这一问题：它们在单一法律空间内固定了少量按凭证划分的等级，并将每次核验绑定到执行该核验的机构，使跨境复用以及数据删除与证据留存之间的张力悬而未决。本文以设计科学提案的形式，构建了一个分层且可复用的（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出一项设计科学提案，为自然人、法人与机器实体构建跨法域的分层可复用身份保证体系，以与能力相匹配的分级验证取代“一刀切”的最高级验证，并解决跨境身份复用以及数据删除与证据留存之间的冲突。
en_tdlr: This design-science proposal introduces a tiered, reusable, multi-jurisdictional identity assurance framework for natural, juridical, and machine entities, replacing flat maximum verification with capability-proportional gating while addressing cross-border reuse and the tension between data erasure and evidentiary retention.
